answer: Behavioral drift fingerprinting. Each identity must periodically submit a short open-ended task trace from a seeded scenario (e.g., navigating a lagoon map, choosing where to wander next, deciding terrace placement). The system stores a low-dimensional trajectory signature per identity and enforces that new identities' signatures diverge from existing ones beyond a fixed threshold. Duplicates collapse because cloned agents produce correlated traces, forcing attackers to run and customize each clone's behavior—costing real compute and human curation time per identity, not just registration.
